current.text: Caleb Wilson is a rookie. Chicago took him with the No. 4 overall pick.
He is in Chicago's projected starting five with Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis and Nic Claxton.

Experts expect low usage as a rookie, about 30 minutes at roughly 20 percent usage or less. Powell, Buzelis and Giddey should all get more usage, and the Bulls are not expected to push his offensive role much.
Experts project him as the second-best rookie this season.
Experts say he is fine in the 80s but his ESPN rank of 56 is too high. A top 100 season would be a good result for him, and going at pick 89 is good value.
In summer league he averaged 22 points and 7 rebounds on 37 percent usage and shot 42 percent on 8 threes a game. His shooting fell off as summer league went on.
Experts call his summer league shooting partly fool's gold. They expect rocky efficiency early, maybe only about 30 percent from three this season, so his early value should come from defense.
Lineups with Claxton and Giddey should have poor spacing, and the team lacks shooting.
Drafting him next to Zach Edey takes away a lot of his upside.
New head coach Tiago Splitter has replaced Billy Donovan. Experts expect him to push the young players and open up their roles.
With a March 28 end, Chicago plays 3, 3 and 4 games (10 total) in our playoff weeks. The team has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from rebounds, blocks and steals. Blocks and rebounds are his best categories for a forward.
Shooting is his weak point. He is a poor free throw shooter, and his three-point shooting is a concern.
He is not expected to give many assists. Experts worry about tunnel vision and doubt his passing.
He was a low-usage player in college and rarely shot threes there. In summer league he took many threes.
He is a good finisher and athlete.
Long term he probably leans more to defense than to offense, but the gap should narrow.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues because his defensive stats count less in points formats.

note: Experts rank Wilson in the 80s for categories. That matches his Yahoo rank of 85 and Yahoo average cost of 2.6 USD, not his ESPN rank of 56 or ESPN cost of 5.1 USD. In our 144-player auction he is a cheap buy in the single digits, up to about his Yahoo value of 10 USD. His projected 7.7 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game help builds that need rebounds and blocks from a forward, at a small cost in FT% (74.8) and turnovers. Early in the season, check his usage next to Powell, Buzelis and Giddey, and whether his three-point attempts and FT% hold up.
